<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par124 />So especially {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים|translate=Godhead, God}} (to be distinguished from the numerical plural ''gods'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=12}}, &c.). The supposition that {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים}} is to be regarded as merely a remnant of earlier polytheistic views (i.e. as originally only a numerical plural) is at least highly improbable, and, moreover, would not explain the analogous plurals (see below). That the language has entirely rejected the idea of numerical plurality in {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים}} (whenever it denotes ''one'' God), is proved especially by its being almost invariably joined with a singular attribute (cf. {{GHGpar|132|h}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים צַדִּיק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=7|verse=10}}, &c. Hence {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים}} may have been used originally not only as a numerical but also as an abstract plural (corresponding to the Latin ''numen'', and our ''Godhead''), and, like other abstracts of the same kind, have been transferred to a concrete single god (even of the heathen).

{{GHGmargin-letter|124|h}}
To the same class (and probably formed on the analogy of {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים}}) belong the plurals {{GHGheb|text=קְדֹשִׁים|translate=the Most Holy}} (only of Yahweh), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=12|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=9|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=30|verse=3|hidebook=1}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים קְדֹשִׁים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=24|verse=19}}, and the Aram. {{GHGheb|text=עֶלְיוֹנִין|translate=the Most High}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=7|verse=18}}, 22, 25); and probably {{GHGheb|text=תְּרָפִים}} (usually taken in the sense of ''penates'') the image of a god, used especially for obtaining oracles. Certainly in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=13}}, 16 only ''one'' image is intended; in most other places a single image ''may'' be intended<ref>Even in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=34}}, notwithstanding the plural suffix in {{GHGheb|text=וַתְּשִׂמֵם}} and {{GHGheb|text=עֲלֵיהֶם}}, since the construction of these abstracts as numerical plurals is one of the peculiarities of the E-document of the Hexateuch; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=20|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=35|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, and {{GHGpar|145|i}}.</ref>; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=10|verse=2}} alone is it most naturally taken as a numerical plural. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=5|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=גְּבֹהִים|translate=supremus}} (of God) is doubtful; according to others it is a numerical plural, ''superiores''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|124|i}}
Further, {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנִים}}, as well as the singular {{GHGheb|text=אָדוֹן}}, (lordship) ''lord'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנִים קָשֶׁה|translate=a cruel lord}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=19|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנֵי הָאָ֫רֶץ|translate=the lord of the land}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=30}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=19}}; so especially with the suffixes of the 2nd and 3rd persons {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנֶ֫יךָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנַ֫יִךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=45|verse=12}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנָיו}}, &c., also {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנֵ֫ינוּ}} (except {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=16}}); but in 1st sing. always {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנִי}}.<ref>On {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנָי}} (for {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנִי}}) as a name of God, cf. {{GHGpar|135|q}}.</ref> So also {{GHGheb|text=בְּעָלִים}} (with suffixes) ''lord, master'' (of slaves, cattle, or inanimate things; but in the sense of ''maritus'', always in the singular), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בְּעָלָיו}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=3}}, &c.<ref>Euting, ''Reise in Arabien'', p. 61, mentions the interesting fact that the subjects of the Emir of Ḥâyel commonly speak of their ruler as ''šiyûkh'', a plur. majestatis= ''the great sheikh''.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|124|k}}
On the other hand, we must regard as doubtful a number of participles in the plural, which, being used as attributes of God, resemble ''plurales excellentiae''; thus, {{GHGheb|text=עֹשָׂי|translate=my Maker}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=35|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=עֹשַׂ֫יִךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=54|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=עֹשָׂיו}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=149|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=עֹשֶׂיהָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=נֽוֹטֵיהֶם|translate=stretching them out}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=5}}; for all these forms may also be explained as singular, according to {{GHGpar|93|ss}}.<ref>{{GHGheb|text=בֹּֽעֲלַ֫יִךְ}}, which in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=54|verse=5}} is in parallelism with {{GHGheb|text=עֹשַׂ֫יִךְ}}, must then be explained as merely formed on analogy.</ref>—{{GHGheb|text=נֹֽגְשָׂיו}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=12}} might also be regarded as another instance, unless it be a numerical plural, ''their oppressors''; moreover, {{GHGheb|text=מְרִימָיו|translate=him who lifteth it up}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=15}} (but read probably {{GHGheb|text=מְרִימוֹ}}); {{GHGheb|text=שֹֽׁלְחָיו|translate=him who sendeth him}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=10|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=22|verse=21|hidebook=1}} (so Baer, but Ginsburg {{GHGheb|text=שֹֽׁלְחֶ֫ךָ}}), 25:13 (in parallelism with {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנָיו}}). These latter plurals, however (including {{GHGheb|text=מרימיו}}), may probably be more simply explained as indicating an indefinite individual, cf. ''o'' below.—For {{GHGheb|text=שֹֽׁמְרֶ֫יךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=121|verse=5}} (textus receptus) and {{GHGheb|text=בּֽוֹרְאֶ֫יךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=12|verse=1}} (textus receptus) the singular should be read, with Baer.
